body:
_Original comment by_ **holger krekel (BitBucket: [hpk42](http://bitbucket.org/hpk42), GitHub: [hpk42](http://github.com/hpk42))**:

---

What about making `pytest.skip` fail when a function object is passed and point to "pytest.mark.skipif" and the docs?

_Original comment by_ **Floris Bruynooghe (BitBucket: [flub](http://bitbucket.org/flub), GitHub: [flub](http://github.com/flub))**:

---

Sounds like a reasonable solution to me.

_Original comment by_ **Kiril Vladimiroff (BitBucket: [Vladimiroff](http://bitbucket.org/Vladimiroff), GitHub: [Vladimiroff](http://github.com/Vladimiroff))**:

---

If there is going to be a check like this why not simply do `pytest.mark.skipif(True, msg)` if a function object is passed to `pytest.skip`?

_Original comment by_ **Bryce Lampe (BitBucket: [blampe](http://bitbucket.org/blampe), GitHub: [blampe](http://github.com/blampe))**:

---

I agree with Kiril. I think there's value in an unconditional skip, and I've seen several people assume that this is the existing behavior.

_Original comment by_ **holger krekel (BitBucket: [hpk42](http://bitbucket.org/hpk42), GitHub: [hpk42](http://github.com/hpk42))**:

---

From a API design perspective I dislike mixing pytest.mark.skipif and pytest.skip because it mixes a "declarative" (mark it as being skipped) and an "imperative" (skip it now) way of doing things.  Bailing out with a clear error, pointing to use "mark.skipif" allows to keep the conceptual separation which is better in the long run IMO.

_Original comment by_ **Kiril Vladimiroff (BitBucket: [Vladimiroff](http://bitbucket.org/Vladimiroff), GitHub: [Vladimiroff](http://github.com/Vladimiroff))**:

---

Fair point, but from usage perspective I find it awkward to do `@pytest.mark.skipif(True, reason="...")` instead of `@pytest.skip`.

_Original comment by_ **Bryce Lampe (BitBucket: [blampe](http://bitbucket.org/blampe), GitHub: [blampe](http://github.com/blampe))**:

---

> Bailing out with a clear error, pointing to use "mark.skipif" allows to keep the conceptual separation which is better in the long run IMO.

I don't think there is any such conceptual separation _for users of the API_, though. This is largely because
- Both methods can already be used declaratively, giving the _appearance_ that this works as expected.
- Declarative syntax for `@pytest.skip` mimics [existing libraries](https://docs.python.org/2/library/unittest.html#skipping-tests-and-expected-failures).

In fact, writing `@pytest.mark.skipif(True, ...` is _so_ awkward that I regularly see people use `@unittest.skip` instead, only because it does what they need, it's compatible with pytest methods, and they're aware of this bug. I say give the people what they want :)

_Original comment by_ **Anatoly Bubenkov (BitBucket: [bubenkoff](http://bitbucket.org/bubenkoff), GitHub: [bubenkoff](http://github.com/bubenkoff))**:

---

I agree with Holger on that it's bad idea to mix conceptions
I would stick to markers approach:
introduce new marker - pytest.mark.skip(reason=None), which is a shortcut of pytest.mark.skipif(True, reason=reason)
this way we'll simplify the easy task of skipping certain test
and then let's strictly prevent using pytest.skip as a decorator

_Original comment by_ **Floris Bruynooghe (BitBucket: [flub](http://bitbucket.org/flub), GitHub: [flub](http://github.com/flub))**:

---

I think the case is made that the `pytest.skip()` API is a little confusing with respect to people migrating from other unittest frameworks.  However I also think that making `pytest.skip()` work as a decorator breaks py.test's consistency where the clear pattern is that all decorators to be applied on test functions are `@pytest.mark.xxx`.  I think starting to break this now will just make confusion worse rather then better.

So with that in mind I am also in favour of detecting `@pytest.skip` and referring to `@pytest.mark.skip` (I think @bubenkoff's idea of that shortcut might be a good plan) as @hpk42 suggests.

If that is still too confusing the I'd suggest that py.test should drop the `pytest.skip()` and `pytest.fail()` API completely, going with `raise pytest.SkipException(msg)` and `raise pytest.FailException(msg)` instead but that's majorly backwards-incompatible so not a very viable thing either.

_Original comment by_ **Anatoly Bubenkov (BitBucket: [bubenkoff](http://bitbucket.org/bubenkoff), GitHub: [bubenkoff](http://github.com/bubenkoff))**:

---

that's not how it works im affraid
we cannot just merge it 'until'
but you can create another PR implementing discussed solution :)

issue.title: pytest.skip doesn't do what we want.

repository.name: splash
repository.description: Lightweight, scriptable browser as a service with an HTTP API

issue.body:
Hey @kmike,
#272 actually doesn't do what I expected. `pytest.skip` actually skips all the tests in the file. It's an issue in pytest https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/issues/607. I managed to missed that somehow.

issue.title: Add pytest.mark.skip shortcut (Issue #607)

repository.name: pytest
repository.description: The pytest framework makes it easy to write small tests, yet scales to support complex functional testing

issue.body:
Add a non-conditional skip marker for convenience as requested in Issue #607. 

I will also probably be adding another feature which automatically treats `@pytest.skip` as `pytest.mark.skip` if it detects itself being used as a decorator. I was thinking that this should probably be opened as a separate pull request though unless you don't mind it being included in here?

Ran `python runtox.py -e py27,py34,flakes` to test changes.

This work is a result of the pyconuk pytest sprint! :)

body: FWIW the implementation for `pytest.mark.skip` was just merged in the `features` branch, target for the `2.9` release. :smile:
